advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix stage classification so a finalizer failure after a partially-exhausted evidence phase is still reported as stage="finalizer", not "evidence".
evidence: 684: elif len(evidence) == len(expected) and not any(e.get("exhausted") for e in evidence):
message interpolates stage: 714: f"{stage} recovery also failed; increasing max_tokens alone cannot "

A finalizer failure (e.g. _validate_coverage raising CompletionRecoveryError, or a finalizer runner error) after one exhausted criterion has len(evidence)==len(expected) but any(exhausted)==True, so the elif is skipped and stage becomes 'evidence' — mislabeling where the failure actually occurred.
advisory.finding: When the finalizer run fails after at least one criterion was exhausted (all N criteria have evidence entries, but one is a placeholder), the outer handler classifies the failure as stage="evidence" rather than "finalizer". The pre-fix logic classified any run with all-N entries as a finalizer-stage failure; the new guard `and not any(e.get("exhausted"))` demotes a true finalizer failure to "evidence", producing a misleading diagnostic and error message ('bounded evidence recovery also failed').
scenarios: N-criterion recovery where one evidence run exhausted (placeholder appended) and the tool-free finalizer subsequently raises or fails coverage validation.
advisory.suggested_fix: Track finalizer entry explicitly (e.g. a `reached_finalizer` flag set true just before the finalizer runner.run) and base the finalizer-stage decision on that flag rather than on the absence of exhausted entries, so an exhausted criterion no longer masks a genuine finalizer-stage failure.

evidence: src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:684 `elif len(evidence) == len(expected) and not any(e.get("exhausted") for e in evidence):` — new branch sets stage='finalizer' only when no entry is exhausted; otherwise falls to stage='evidence'

tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_recovery_evidence_ed6d.py asserts exhausted counts, placeholder content, and all-exhausted counts, but no test makes the finalizer FAIL after a partial exhaustion and asserts failure_diagnostic['stage']=='evidence'

ABSENCE: search of tests/unit/workflow for 'stage' shows no ed6d test asserting the stage field; existing stage assertions live in other tickets' tests and do not cover the mixed partial-exhaustion + finalizer-failure path
advisory.finding: The stage-classification branch introduced by this diff (finalizer stage now requires that no evidence entry is exhausted) is not covered by any test: no test drives a finalizer-stage failure AFTER a partial per-criterion exhaustion, which is exactly the case the new `and not any(e.get('exhausted') ...)` clause distinguishes. A regression that mis-classified this case (e.g. reverting to the old `stage='finalizer' if len(evidence)==len(expected)`) would not be caught.
scenarios: Two criteria succeed, one exhausts (placeholder), then the finalizer runner.run raises an LLMError — the diagnostic should now report stage='evidence', not 'finalizer'
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test: runner fails one evidence index with _budget_exc() (placeholder), succeeds the rest, then raises an LLMError from the structured/finalizer run; assert pytest.raises(CompletionRecoveryError) and step.failure_diagnostic['stage']=='evidence'.

advisory.finding: The token-exhaustion placeholder path is asserted only by exhausted-count, not by placeholder content: the UnretryableOutputError used carries no .diagnostic, so the placeholder renders 'requests=None, tool_calls=None'. No test asserts the placeholder text for an exhaustion exception lacking numeric counters, leaving the None-rendering of _run_criterion_evidence's placeholder unverified.
scenarios: A token-exhaustion UnretryableOutputError with no diagnostic produces a placeholder embedding literal 'None' counters that could later be misread or break downstream parsing

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Omit or default the counter clause in the exhausted placeholder when requests/tool_calls are absent, instead of interpolating 'None'.
evidence: tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_recovery_evidence_ed6d.py: _runaway_exc uses diagnostic={"requests": 55, "distinct_ratio_window": 0.5} (no tool_calls), so tool_calls renders as None
_bounded_diagnostic initializes requests/tool_calls to None (lines 286-287) and only overwrites them when present in the exception.
dropped.finding: The exhausted placeholder text renders `requests=None`/`tool_calls=None` verbatim when the caught exception carries a diagnostic lacking those keys (e.g. a RunawayToolLoopError whose diagnostic has distinct_ratio_window but no tool_calls, as in the test's _runaway_exc). The placeholder then advertises 'requests=None, tool_calls=None', which is noise rather than the intended numeric usage counters.
scenarios: RunawayToolLoopError or any exhaustion exception whose diagnostic omits requests or tool_calls.
